topic: Embedding storage type and indexing
detail: Missing: A short, prominent statement in the vector-search docs and sample quickstarts that explicitly says: 'Vectors must be stored as number[] (an array of numbers) to be indexed by cosmosSearch; packing embeddings into BSON Binary will not be indexed.' The repository README mentions packed-Binary but does not make this caution prominent. Looked in: documentdb-vector-search skill, 'Integrated vector store' Microsoft docs, sample README and code; discover step found the number[] requirement but the sample still stored Binary. Effect: The builder followed the prompt and stored binary-packed embeddings; as a result server-side vector indexing will likely not work and the sample falls back to in-memory ranking. This reduces the sample's value as a demonstration of server-side vector-ivf search.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add a short 'Indexable vector storage' note to the top of the 'Vector search' documentation and to the sample README. Example text: 'Important: To be indexed by DocumentDB's cosmosSearch vector indexes, store vectors as an array of numbers (e.g., embedding: [0.123, ...]). Storing embeddings as BSON Binary (packed float32) is compact but will not be indexed. If you must store Binary for offline use, also persist a number[] copy or use a separate index pipeline.'

For production datasets compute nlist ~ max(1, N/1000) and document the heuristic.' Include a small code snippet showing how to compute nlist from collection.count_documents({}).

topic: IVF numLists sizing
detail: Violated: When using IVF, choose numLists relative to dataset size (use documentCount/1000 for up to ~1M documents, and consider other index types like DiskANN beyond that); tune nProbes to trade recall for latency. Evidence: app/scripts/create_vector_index.py:27-31 (cosmosSearchOptions.options: {'nlist': 100}) — nlist=100 is not tuned relative to dataset size (demo has 5 documents).
proposed_change: Set a conservative demo default (e.g., nlist = min(32, max(1, document_count//1000))) or compute nlist from collection count; document the heuristic in the index script.

topic: Embedding storage type
detail: Violated: Store vectors as numeric arrays (number[]) so they can be indexed; embedding values stored as other types (for example raw BSON Binary) are not accepted by the vector index and will not be indexed. Evidence: app/scripts/load_data.py:79-83 (packs normalized float32 into Binary and sets doc['embedding'] = Binary(packed)); app/app.py uses Binary in searches (pack_embedding/unpack functions).
proposed_change: Store embeddings as a numeric array: doc['embedding'] = vec.tolist() (float32), and update create_vector_index/aggregation usage accordingly. Update README to warn builders that Binary-packed embeddings will not be indexed by cosmosSearch.

topic: Prefer Entra ID for auth
detail: Violated: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC) + role-based access control for cluster authentication and management rather than embedding long-lived cluster passwords in code; Entra ID can be enabled as an auth mode on the cluster and you can register service principals or managed identities. Evidence: The sample uses MONGO_URI connection strings and .env.example; README does not document Entra ID usage or why it is not used in the demo.
proposed_change: Add a README section showing how to use Microsoft Entra ID (example with azure-identity and PyMongo MONGODB-OIDC) or state clearly why the sample uses connection-string auth for the quickstart.

topic: Retries & 429 handling
detail: Violated: Handle transient errors and rate limits with retries and exponential backoff, and treat HTTP 429 / rate-limiting specially (respect any Retry-After header and instrument throttling metrics). Evidence: app/app.py and scripts/load_data.py do not implement retries or exponential backoff around MongoClient operations or embedding API calls; the code catches exceptions but does not retry.
proposed_change: Add retry wrappers with exponential backoff (respect Retry-After for 429s) around db.command, coll.aggregate and OpenAI calls; consider using tenacity or similar retry libs.

topic: Verify index availability
detail: Violated: Verify index creation and availability before sending search traffic (make index creation idempotent and check listIndexes/getIndexes or createIndexes response). Evidence: app/scripts/create_vector_index.py prints the payload and attempts db.command but there is no code that verifies the index exists before the Flask app starts or prevents searches while index build/incompatibility exists. app/app.py relies on catching exceptions at query time and falling back to in-memory ranking (app/app.py:101-121, 122-146).
proposed_change: Modify create_vector_index.py to check getIndexes/listIndexes and block/return error until index is 'ready', or add an app startup check that refuses $search until index is present. Persist the admin payload if the gateway rejects the command.

topic: Binary artifacts & indexing
detail: Violated: If you choose to store embedding-related binary artifacts for non-index use (for example compact on-disk storage), document the serialization format and be aware that the DocumentDB vector index requires number[] for indexing so binary blobs won't be queryable by cosmosSearch. Evidence: app/scripts/load_data.py writes Binary(packed float32) (line 81). README.md:46 documents packing as 'BSON Binary (packed float32 little-endian)' but does not clearly say this will not be indexed by cosmosSearch.
proposed_change: Either store as number[] so server-side indexing works, or (if Binary is required) explicitly document the choice and note that such Binary embeddings will not be indexed by cosmosSearch (and give the alternative indexing approach).

topic: Unique indexes / idempotent seed

Evidence: seed.js inserts products and orders with insertMany (app/src/seed.js lines 133-145, 150-166) but seed does not create unique index on productId or upsert logic; a repeated run may create duplicates if insertMany doesn't rely on _id uniqueness or if the collection's unique index isn't set.

topic: Embed metadata

topic: Validate vector dims

There's no explicit per-document dims check.
proposed_change: Add a pre-insert check in seed.js that validates embedding.length === EMBEDDING_DIMS and rejects or pads/truncates inconsistent vectors with an explicit log/error.

topic: Retry semantics

proposed_change: Wrap network/DB calls in a retry helper that honors Retry-After and uses exponential backoff with jitter; for bulk ingest, throttle concurrency and implement retries for 429 responses.

topic: Partial index for uncategorized
detail: Violated: Use partial indexes (partialFilterExpression) to index only the subset of documents your query filters on to reduce index size and write cost (e.g., index only documents where category does not exist). Evidence: app/scripts/seed.js line 9 creates index { date: 1, category: 1 } but no partial index on category:{ $exists:false } is created.
proposed_change: Create a partial index for categorization scans, e.g. coll.createIndex({ date:1, category:1 }, { partialFilterExpression: { category: { $exists: false } } }) in the seed script.

topic: Idempotent categorization updates
detail: Violated: Make categorization updates idempotent by using conditional updates (e.g. filter { _id:..., category: { $exists: false } } and $set the category), avoiding blind re-writes so multiple runs won't overwrite audited labels. Evidence: app/src/index.js lines 30-33 and app/scripts/run_categorization.js lines 11-14 call updateOne({ _id: doc._id }, { $set: { category } }) without a conditional filter to ensure category doesn't already exist. The code fetches only uncategorized docs in the query, but the update itself is blind and would overwrite if concurrency or race conditions occur.
proposed_change: Use a conditional update filter to make updates atomic and idempotent, e.g. coll.updateOne({ _id: doc._id, category: { $exists: false } }, { $set: { category } }).

topic: Resume tokens
detail: Violated: Persist change-stream resume tokens durably and resume the stream with resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime to continue from the last processed event. Evidence: No code persists resume tokens. change stream is opened without resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime (app/src/worker/watch.js and app/src/alert_watcher.js show watch() calls but no token persistence).
proposed_change: Persist the last processed change._id (resume token) to a durable collection on every processed event and call Model.watch(..., { resumeAfter: token }) on restart; implement exponential backoff and safe resume failure handling.

topic: Short handlers
detail: Violated: Keep change-stream handlers short and offload webhook delivery or expensive evaluation to background workers/queues. Evidence: app/src/worker/watch.js and app/src/alert_watcher.js perform synchronous HTTP requests (await axios.post or await sendWebhook) inside the change stream handler rather than enqueuing work.
proposed_change: Offload webhook delivery to a background worker or message queue; in the short term, perform non-blocking enqueue (e.g., write delivery requests to a 'deliveries' collection and process them with a separate worker) so the watch loop returns quickly.

topic: Compound index ESR

Evidence: Alert-rule queries use userId + active + symbol semantics; existing indexes include userId and userId+active but not a full { userId:1, active:1, symbol:1 } compound index to cover the common predicate, so some queries may still require extra work. (app/src/models/alertrule.js shows defined indexes.)
proposed_change: Add a compound index on { userId: 1, active: 1, symbol: 1 } to avoid scans when matching rules by userId, active and symbol.

topic: allowDiskUse

proposed_change: Pass { allowDiskUse: true } to aggregate when running larger datasets or document this option in README and conditionally enable it when result size may exceed memory.

topic: Retries and backoff

proposed_change: Add exponential-backoff retry helper for transient DB and webhook errors and persist failed webhooks to a 'dead-letter' collection after retry exhaustion.

I reviewed the prompt_review and skills for best-practice guidance but no single canonical choice is enforced; this remains a builder decision.
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: Sample earnings-call PDFs and licensing
detail: The prompt asks to ingest earnings-call PDFs but does not include a sample transcript or specify a public data source/license. I searched the quickstarts and skills and found no bundled sample. The builder must supply or document sample PDFs (with appropriate license) or provide a script that accepts user-supplied PDFs.
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: Idempotent seed script and record deduplication
detail: The prompt requires ingesting documents and creating indexes but does not require an idempotent seed script. The skills and docs explain insert/bulk operations but don't provide a canonical, idempotent sample ingestion pattern that detects and skips already-ingested chunks. The builder must choose a chunk_id scheme and implement dedupe explicitly.
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: DocumentDB Agent Kit (npx skills add Azure/documentdb-agent-kit)
detail: Exists and would have sped this build up, but was not installed.
proposed_change: Mention it in the kit's setup skill, or make the pipeline install it.

topic: mongosh
detail: Install mongosh on the developer machine to run ad-hoc queries, inspect indexes and test aggregation pipelines locally against the cluster. Install from MongoDB's official distributions (or package manager) and use it with --tlsAllowInvalidCertificates when connecting to local gateway for dev. If not added, rely on the documentdb MCP server for index and query inspection.
proposed_change: Install mongosh on the developer machine to run ad-hoc queries, inspect indexes and test aggregation pipelines locally against the cluster. Install from MongoDB's official distributions (or package manager) and use it with --tlsAllowInvalidCertificates when connecting to local gateway for dev. If not added, rely on the documentdb MCP server for index and query inspection.

topic: Embedding model & index-dimension selection
detail: Missing: No canonical guidance page that tells sample builders which embedding models and dimensions to pick for DocumentDB RAG samples (e.g., 'use all-MiniLM-L6-v2 → dims=384' vs OpenAI 1536-dim models) and how to change the vector index dims. Looked in: DocumentDB skills, Microsoft Learn quickstarts, and the agent-kit skill resources (documentdb-vector-search, vector-create-diskann-index.md). Effect: Builder picked all-MiniLM-L6-v2 by default and documented dims=384 in README; index creation was left to the operator. The lack of a single recommended model+dims made the builder log a model_default decision (D005) and reduced automation.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short 'Embedding model choices for RAG on DocumentDB' page that (a) lists example models (local miniLM 384, OpenAI 1536), (b) maps each model to the index 'dimensions' value, (c) includes a sample createIndexes JSON for each dims value and index kind, and (d) recommends which models to use for small demo vs production.

topic: Create vector index: exact createIndexes JSON and how to run it
detail: Missing: A discoverable example that copies the exact createIndexes payload for DocumentDB (cosmosSearchOptions) and a small script that runs it idempotently via MCP or mongosh. Looked in: documentdb-vector-search skill, Microsoft Learn vector-search docs, sample repo README. Effect: Builder recorded the required JSON in the run notes and README, but could not create the index via MCP in this environment. Without a copy-paste-able createIndexes JSON and an idempotent script the user must hand-construct index creation steps in the portal.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add an example file 'examples/create_vector_index.json' with the exact createIndexes payload for DiskANN/HNSW/IVF, a small Python script that calls the MCP helper if enabled, and a README section 'How to create the vector index (pasteable JSON)'.

topic: Context-engineering heuristics for DocumentDB RAG
detail: Missing: No documented, service-specific guidance on assembling passages within the LLM token budget (rank by score, distinct timestamps, token-counting examples). Looked in: General RAG literature and DocumentDB skills; searches for 'context engineering' and 'DocumentDB RAG context window' returned no service-specific guidance. Effect: Builder did not implement token-budget-aware selection (requirement missed) and instead concatenated top-k passages, risking out-of-context or truncated prompts when used with real LLMs.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A page 'Context assembly for RAG on DocumentDB' with a recommended algorithm (token estimator, answer buffer, score-based greedy selection with timestamp diversity), code snippet (Python) and an example with tiktoken to compute tokens.

topic: Idempotent seed-ingest pattern
detail: Missing: A canonical, idempotent ingestion pattern (bulk upserts or bulk ReplaceOne with upsert=True) and sample code for doing bulk upserts efficiently against DocumentDB. Looked in: Quickstart insert docs and agent-kit skills; no small canonical example for idempotent chunked ingestion was found. Effect: Builder implemented deterministic chunk_id and a unique index (good), but insert_many produces DuplicateKeyErrors on rerun (caught but noisy).
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] A short 'Idempotent ingestion' sample illustrating creating deterministic chunk IDs and using pymongo.bulk_write with ReplaceOne(filter={'chunk_id':...}, replacement=doc, upsert=True) and showing how to batch and resume.

topic: Index/management tool discoverability & opt-in flags
detail: Missing: Clear guidance on when and how to enable the DocumentDB MCP management/write tools (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS / ENABLE_WRITE_TOOLS) that the agent helpers rely on. Looked in: Events and MCP skill docs; the run environment reported management tools are disabled and the error message refers to environment flags but the README doesn't say how to opt in. Effect: Builder attempted to create indexes and insert documents using MCP helpers and those calls failed in this environment; the lack of opt-in docs prevented the build from fully verifying index creation and server-side vector queries.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] An agent-kit rule and small README section: 'To allow automation to create indexes and insert test data, set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true and ENABLE_WRITE_TOOLS=true in your environment (only enable in trusted contexts). Example: export ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true'.

topic: Retry/backoff guidance for SDK & embedding calls
detail: Missing: An explicit, service-specific retry/backoff recipe for DocumentDB writes, index builds and embedding-provider calls (include 429 handling and idempotent writes). Looked in: documentdb-connection skill and general docs; no ready-to-copy recipe for sample authors. Effect: No retry/backoff is implemented in sample; transient failures will surface as unhandled exceptions or noisy messages.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] Add a short page 'Retries and idempotency for DocumentDB' with example code (tenacity wrapper), recommended retry counts and backoff policy, and example of combining retries with upsert semantics.

topic: Context: LLM provider & local dev guidance (token budgets)
detail: Missing: Repository doesn't document the LLM model choices, token budgets, or how to adapt the context-engineering logic to local vs hosted LLMs. Looked in: repo README and skills. Effect: Builder left LLM selection to a model_default decision and did not implement token-aware assembly.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add a short 'LLM choices and token budgets' README subsection describing OpenAI/davinci vs local LlamaIndex, expected context sizes, and example token budgets/answer buffer sizes.

topic: PDF ingestion example
detail: Missing: A tiny, permissively licensed PDF transcript example and an in-repo PDF->text example (pdfminer.six) so builders can demonstrate PDF ingestion in a minimal, legal way. Looked in: repo samples and public quickstarts. Effect: Builder included a plaintext sample only and documented that PDF support is not implemented; users must supply PDFs and implement parsing themselves.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] Provide an example script 'tools/pdf_to_text.py' that demonstrates extracting timestamped lines from a sample PDF using pdfminer.six (with instructions about licensing).

topic: Unit tests & offline mocks for DocumentDB RAG samples
detail: Missing: A recommended test scaffold (pytest) and examples that mock MongoDB and embedding models so tests run without a live cluster. Looked in: repo and skill docs. Effect: No tests exist; this makes CI for the sample harder and forces manual verification against a live cluster.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] Add a tests/ directory with pytest tests that use mongomock for collection behavior and a stubbed embedding provider that returns deterministic vectors. Show how to run tests (pytest) without cloud access.

topic: Clarify product naming & CLI/Bicep snippets
detail: Missing: Some older docs and snippets in the ecosystem confuse DocumentDB with Cosmos DB databaseAccounts. Builders need a single authoritative note indicating 'use Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters for vCore clusters' and 'use az documentdb mongocluster' CLI group. Looked in: readiness findings and the 'service confusions' entries in the readiness report. Effect: If builders copy generic Cosmos DB examples they will choose wrong IaC resource types and incorrect CLI groups. The sample avoids auto-provisioning, so the immediate build was not broken, but automation could fail.
proposed_change: [naming_or_disambiguation] Add a one-paragraph 'Which resource to use' note to the README plus exact Bicep/az CLI example(s) showing Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters and az documentdb mongocluster commands.

topic: Require TLS
detail: Violated: Require TLS for all connections (connection strings include tls=true) and restrict network access with firewall rules or Private Endpoints. Evidence: src/db.py (lines 12-17) simply passes the URI through to MongoClient; there is no check that tls=true or tls/ssl options are present, nor guidance to enforce Private Endpoint usage in the code.
proposed_change: Validate DOCUMENTDB_URI in get_client() and warn/raise if TLS is not requested (or document that the URI should include tls=true), and add README guidance on network protection.

topic: Least-privilege credentials
detail: Violated: Give application credentials least privilege: create a database-scoped user for the sample app instead of using an admin key or cluster-wide credentials. Evidence: The sample expects a full connection string in DOCUMENTDB_URI (src/db.py line 15). There is no guidance or helper that creates or recommends a DB-scoped user or demonstrates connecting via Microsoft Entra ID/ODIC.
proposed_change: Add README instructions showing how to create a least-privilege database user scoped to sample_fintech_04, or add an example using Microsoft Entra ID OIDC if the cluster supports it.

topic: Conventional indexes for filters
detail: Violated: Also create conventional single-field or compound indexes on frequently filtered fields (e.g., transcript_id, source, chunk_id, start_time). Evidence: src/ingest.py (lines 43-46) creates only a unique index on chunk_id (coll.create_index([('chunk_id',1)], unique=True)). There are no indexes on source or start_time.
proposed_change: Create indexes on 'source' and 'start_time' (or a compound index including transcript/source + start_time) so transcript/time-range filters are efficient.

topic: Use cluster's vector search API
detail: Violated: Run nearest-neighbor queries using the cluster's vector search API (cosmosSearch / $search) with topK and tune search parameters. Evidence: src/query.py (lines 25-40) pulls documents and computes cosine locally; it does not use $search/cosmosSearch aggregation (no server-side vector search call).
proposed_change: When a vector index exists, switch the retrieval path to use $search + cosmosSearch aggregation with topK and $project to fetch only needed fields; keep client-side fallback for local testing.

topic: Metadata pre-filtering
detail: Violated: Apply metadata-based pre-filtering (for example by transcript/source or date range) as part of or before vector search to reduce fan-out and RU/IO costs. Evidence: src/query.py (line 29) only filters on embedding_model in the find call; it does not accept or apply a transcript/source or date-range filter.
proposed_change: Support optional --source or --date-range flags and include them as filters in the aggregation/$search call or in the prefilter find query to reduce candidate set.

topic: Retries and backoff
detail: Violated: Implement exponential backoff and retries for transient network errors and throttling (429), and make writes idempotent so retries don't create duplicates. Evidence: No retry/backoff behavior is present around database writes or embedding calls in src/ingest.py or src/query.py.
proposed_change: Wrap network/DB calls with a retry/backoff wrapper (e.g., tenacity) and ensure upsert semantics for write retries.

topic: Prefer built-in vector search
detail: Violated: Use application-side cosine calculation only as a fallback; prefer built-in vector search APIs for scale and performance. Evidence: src/query.py (lines 25-40) computes cosine similarity in the application over all docs; built-in $search/cosmosSearch is not used.
proposed_change: Add aggregation that calls $search + cosmosSearch when vector index is present; keep client-side scoring for small local datasets.

topic: Sanitize text before embedding
detail: Violated: Sanitize and normalize text before embedding (strip control characters, normalize whitespace, preserve timestamps). Evidence: src/ingest.py (lines 17-35) trims whitespace but does not run control-character sanitization or normalization steps; timestamps are not extracted.
proposed_change: Add a text normalization step before chunking: remove control chars, normalize unicode, collapse whitespace, and extract/preserve inline timestamps; document this in ingest.py and README.

topic: Context-engineering assembly
detail: Violated: Assemble retrieved passages to fit LLM token budget: rank by vector score, concatenate until budget minus answer buffer is reached, prefer distinct timestamps. Evidence: No token-budgeting or timestamp-aware selection exists in src/query.py; the script uses top-k and simple concatenation.
proposed_change: Implement passage selection logic that uses a token estimator (tiktoken or average char→token ratio), reserves an answer buffer, and prefers distinct timestamps if scores are close. Add a README section describing the heuristic.

topic: Create a cosmosSearch vector index (kind vector-ivf, vector-hnsw or vector-diskann) on the embedding field in code, with
detail: partly_met because tool_unavailable. README.md (notes: lines 32-35) documents a vector-diskann index with dimensions=384; the build attempted to call documentdb_create_index but the MCP management tools were disabled (events: documentdb_create_index calls failed, events.jsonl lines ~48-49 show 'Management tools are disabled by default'). The app itself does not programmatically create the vector index.
proposed_change: Add an idempotent index-creation routine that: (a) uses the MCP helper when ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS is set and (b) otherwise prints the exact createIndexes JSON that the user should run (including cosmosSearchOptions with kind and dimensions).

topic: Provide a single-agent question-answering flow that takes an analyst's natural-language question, embeds it and runs a $
detail: partly_met because tool_unavailable. src/query.py (lines 25-40, 63-70) — the sample embeds the query locally and returns top-k by computing cosine similarity in-process over documents pulled from the collection (client-side scoring). It does not call $search / cosmosSearch aggregation on the server.
proposed_change: Add an aggregation path that issues db.collection.aggregate([{ $search: { cosmosSearch: { vector: <queryVec>, path: 'embedding', k: <k> } } }, { $project: { score: { $meta: 'searchScore' }, text:1, source:1, start_time:1 } }]) when a vector index exists; keep the client-side fallback for environments without a vector index.

If the builder stores embeddings as Binary (see S03), the index won't pick them up.

detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with mongodb_atlas_or_server). Build risk: Storing embeddings as BSON Binary will cause the vector index to ignore those documents; semantic search will return no results (the core functionality of the sample would fail).

Effect: Builder recorded the need to read DOCUMENTDB_URI from env but did not publish .env.example. This makes it harder for users to run the sample safely without exposing secrets.

topic: Exchange-rate document indexing pattern
detail: Missing: A public example recommending an ExchangeRate document shape (fromCurrency, toCurrency, rate: Decimal128, effectiveDate) and a compound index { fromCurrency:1, toCurrency:1, effectiveDate:-1 } for latest-rate lookups. Looked in: Searched DocumentDB indexing and data-modeling skills; the general compound-index ESR recipe exists but no canonical currency-pair + effectiveDate example was found. Effect: Builder's design includes exchange rate docs and a compound index but with no public example to cite agents may choose a suboptimal index or model shape and make lookups inefficient.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short doc: 'Modeling exchange rates' with schema, recommended indexes, $lookup example to fetch latest effectiveRate in an aggregation, and a note on TTL or archiving older rates.

topic: Transaction lifetime and retry limits guidance
detail: Missing: Authoritative statement on recommended transaction duration limits and the recommended retry-loop for transactions on Azure DocumentDB with Mongoose (timeouts, backoff). Looked in: Searched skills and Learn pages; readiness_findings flagged missing single-page guidance for transaction lifetime and retry behaviour. Effect: Builder assumed conservative timeouts but did not implement or verify retry/timeouts. Missing guidance risks long-running transactions that get aborted and unexpected failures in production.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A small guidance page: 'Transactions on DocumentDB' stating recommended max duration, how to set timeouts and serverSelectionTimeoutMS, sample retry-loop pattern for transient errors, and a note about keeping transactions short and touching few documents.

topic: Tests that run without live cluster (mocking patterns)
detail: Missing: A documented pattern and example tests that run without a live DocumentDB cluster (in-memory server or mocking Mongoose models) for CI. Looked in: Searched skills and quickstarts; no sample tests were found that demonstrate an offline test harness for DocumentDB-specific features. Effect: No tests were produced; team and agents lack a quick recipe for creating unit tests that don't require the live cluster, slowing CI setup and making regression checks harder.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] Add a tests/ folder with example unit tests using sinon or an in-memory MongoDB library and instructions for which tests require live cluster vs mocked behavior. Include a CI snippet that runs unit tests without network access.

topic: Decimal128 for money
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Store monetary amounts using Decimal128 or integer minor-units; do not use JavaScript Number for currency values.
proposed_change: A short authoritative sentence in the DocumentDB data-modeling docs: 'For monetary values use Decimal128 or integer minor-units; avoid JavaScript Number due to floating-point inaccuracy.'

topic: Mongoose sessions pattern
detail: prior_knowledge_only: When using Mongoose with sessions, pass { session } to all queries/updates and use session.withTransaction or explicit startTransaction/commitTransaction.
proposed_change: A short example page showing Mongoose session usage with DocumentDB, including session.withTransaction and passing { session } to model calls.

The prompt review assumed defaults; the builder must pick and document a provider and model. Looked in installed skills and Microsoft Learn; no authoritative recommendation for model choice was found.
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: Embedding model dimensionality and mapping to vector index dims
detail: The sample needs the embedding model dimension (e.g., 1536) to create vector indexes with the correct 'dimensions' setting. The installed skills describe how to create vector indexes but do not prescribe which embedding model/dimension to use or provide a mapping to available LLM/embedding choices. I searched DocumentDB vector-search docs and agent skills; they list param names but not a recommended embedding model or dims for the sample.
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: Canonical sample document shape / seed data
detail: The prompt leaves collection document shapes (exact field names) unspecified. No skill or Learn page supplies a canonical sample for this sample. The builder should create an idempotent seed script and specify field names for segments (segmentId, name, purchase_history, preferences, optional embedding) and campaigns (segmentId, subject, body, rawOutput, createdAt).
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: mongosh
detail: Install mongosh to speed interactive checks and manual debugging (npm install -g mongosh or use the mongo shell distribution). The DocumentDB quickstarts include mongosh connection examples.
proposed_change: Install mongosh to speed interactive checks and manual debugging (npm install -g mongosh or use the mongo shell distribution). The DocumentDB quickstarts include mongosh connection examples.

topic: LlamaIndex integration guidance
detail: Missing: The starter prompt explicitly asked for a LlamaIndex agent that registers a fetch tool, but no installed skill or public quickstart detailing 'how to wire LlamaIndex to Azure DocumentDB' was found. The builder defaulted to not using LlamaIndex. Looked in: Loaded installed skills (documentdb-*), searched Microsoft Learn for LlamaIndex + DocumentDB examples; no authoritative guide was discovered. Effect: The builder implemented a lightweight agent instead of a LlamaIndex-based agent, causing the build to diverge from the prompt's explicit requirement (the missing item is the primary functional difference).
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Add an agent-kit rule and short sample that shows how to integrate LlamaIndex Node.js with Azure DocumentDB: (1) install LlamaIndex, (2) implement a tool adapter named `fetch_segment` that calls the DocumentDB driver, (3) register the tool with the LlamaIndex agent, and (4) an end-to-end example that seeds segments and runs the LlamaIndex agent to generate a campaign.

topic: Embedding model ↔ vector-index dimensionality mapping
detail: Missing: Public guidance that maps specific embedding model outputs (e.g., OpenAI embeddings dims = 1536) to the vector-index 'dimensions' parameter for DocumentDB was not found in the skill set or Learn quickstarts. Looked in: documentdb-vector-search skill, Microsoft Learn vector search pages, quickstart vector docs. Effect: The builder avoided using vector indexes and embeddings to keep the sample simple; without a published mapping agents cannot safely create vector indexes with the correct 'dimensions' setting.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short Learn page or a section in the vector-search quickstart titled 'Embedding models and DocumentDB index dimensions' that lists common embedding models and their dimensionality (e.g., model X -> 1536) and an example createIndexes JSON block with 'dimensions' set accordingly.

topic: WriteConcern / readPreference mapping for Azure DocumentDB
detail: Missing: Public guidance that states how Azure DocumentDB maps MongoDB writeConcern and readPreference semantics to the managed product and a recommended default for application code. Looked in: Searches for 'Azure DocumentDB writeConcern readPreference' returned no authoritative mapping. Effect: The sample does not set explicit writeConcern/readPreference. An agent cannot confidently change defaults without knowing service behaviour—this could lead to surprising durability or latency mismatches in production.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short page 'Consistency and durability: writeConcern/readPreference' describing supported values, defaults, and sample Node.js driver options to set them safely for typical app needs.

topic: LLM PII handling guidance for prompts
detail: Missing: No public guidance was found that specifically tells agent authors which customer fields are acceptable to send to an LLM when building prompts from DocumentDB data, or sample redaction helpers for Node.js. Looked in: Searches for 'azure documentdb pii lLM redaction' and installed skills. Effect: The sample injects purchase_history into the prompt; absent guidance, an agent may inadvertently send PII to the LLM. The auditor cannot say whether the seeded data contains PII in this sample, so the risk remains.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short 'PII & LLM' guideline for the agent kit and sample README: what fields to redact, sample redaction function (mask email/phone), and a statement recommending encrypting sensitive fields at rest.

topic: Driver versions and supported combinations
detail: Missing: A concise, discoverable list of recommended/pinned Node.js driver versions that are tested and supported against Azure DocumentDB clusters (e.g., supported mongodb Node driver versions). Looked in: Installed skills and Microsoft Learn quickstarts; no single 'supported driver versions' box found. Effect: The sample used mongodb ^5.7.0 and package-lock.json to pin transiently. Agents may not know which driver minor versions are supported; this can cause runtime incompatibilities when new driver versions change behaviour.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add a short 'Supported drivers' section to the quickstart listing tested driver versions per runtime and a recommendation to pin using a lockfile (or add a package.json example with exact versions).

topic: Tests without live cluster (mock patterns)
detail: Missing: Example test harness or pattern that shows how to write unit tests for samples without requiring a live DocumentDB cluster (e.g., using mongodb-memory-server or mocking the MongoClient). Looked in: Installed skills and sample repo. No sample tests or test patterns were found. Effect: The sample contains no tests and the package.json test is a noop; this increases friction for gallery acceptance and automated CI validation.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] Add a short 'Testing' README subsection and an example test file using a mocked MongoClient or mongodb-memory-server showing unit tests for seed/generate functions that pass without a live cluster.

topic: IaC using Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters
detail: Missing: A short IaC snippet for Bicep/ARM/Terraform that shows the correct resource type (Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters) to provision an Azure DocumentDB cluster and minimal safe defaults. Looked in: Learn samples and installed skills; documentation exists but a small ready-to-copy snippet in the sample template was missing. Effect: The sample used an existing cluster (per prompt) so no provisioning was performed; new users may attempt az cosmosdb or azurerm_cosmosdb_account and target the wrong resource type.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add a short 'Optional IaC' file (Bicep) in the sample that demonstrates creating a minimal mongoClusters resource and document the az documentdb mongocluster CLI commands. Link to the Learn template.

topic: .env.example completeness
detail: Missing: .env.example omitted USE_OPENAI (the runtime toggle used by the code). Looked in: app/.env.example and src/generate.js Effect: Operators may be confused why OpenAI is not called by default; small usability gap for developers following README steps.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Update .env.example to include USE_OPENAI=0 and optionally DOCUMENTDB_MAX_POOL_SIZE, ENABLE_WRITE_TOOLS, and any other runtime toggles used by the sample.

topic: Model-default decisions recorded without source
detail: Missing: Some build decisions (D003) were made by model default choices instead of following the prompt (LlamaIndex) and there was no skill or public source that would resolve the choice for an agent. Looked in: decisions.jsonl and the loaded skills; LlamaIndex integration guidance was missing. Effect: The builder diverted from the explicit prompt requirement (no LlamaIndex).
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Add a rule to the agent-kit "If the starter prompt requires a particular library (e.g., LlamaIndex) install and use it, or explicitly record and justify why it was not possible (and prefer to raise a build halt)."

topic: Serverless client pooling
detail: Violated: In serverless environments initialize the MongoClient outside the function handler so the single client and its pool are reused across warm invocations and use small pools (e.g., maxPoolSize 3–5, minPoolSize 0). Evidence: app/src/client.js lines 10-16: client created once, but maxPoolSize is set to 50 (line 13) rather than a small default appropriate for serverless environments.
proposed_change: Make pool-size configurable via env (e.g. DOCUMENTDB_MAX_POOL_SIZE) and default to a small pool (e.g. 5) for serverless deployments.

topic: Entra ID auth
detail: Violated: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC) authentication with a token-callback (DefaultAzureCredential / managed identity) instead of long-lived DB passwords when possible, using the driver's OIDC callback interface to supply tokens. Evidence: app/.env.example (line 2) and src/generate.js/client.js expect a connection string with user:password; README does not document MONGODB-OIDC or managed identity usage.
proposed_change: Document how to use MONGODB-OIDC with managed identity (or provide an example connection string) and/or add code path that obtains tokens via DefaultAzureCredential and uses the driver's OIDC callback.

topic: Monitoring & alerts
detail: Violated: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs and create alerts on CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, and connection saturation appropriate to your cluster tier for production monitoring. Evidence: README and seed/generate scripts do not mention enabling diagnostic settings, slow-query logs or recommended alerts.
proposed_change: Add a short 'Production checklist' section in README that recommends enabling diagnostic settings, slow-query logging and sample alert thresholds for the default M30 tier.

topic: Least-privilege DB users
detail: Violated: Use least-privilege database identities (per-app users or Microsoft Entra RBAC) rather than admin/root credentials for application access. Evidence: app/.env.example suggests a user:password in the connection string but README does not state or demonstrate creating a least-privilege app user or RBAC role for the sample.
proposed_change: Document recommended minimum privileges for the sample and show how to create an app user or configure MONGODB-OIDC with a managed identity for non-admin access.

topic: Retries for transient errors
detail: Violated: Implement retry logic for transient errors and 429 rate-limits with exponential backoff and honor Retry-After when provided. Evidence: Code uses MongoClient with retryWrites: true (src/client.js line 14) but there is no application-level retry/backoff wrapper for transient network errors or 429s around DB operations (seed/generate do not implement retries).
proposed_change: Add an exponential-backoff retry wrapper for DB operations and honor any Retry-After headers returned by the service (or use a supported library wrapper).

topic: Create indexes before seeding
detail: Violated: Create required indexes before seeding or significant reads, and verify indexes at deployment time (listIndexes/listIndexes check) in your provisioning/seed scripts. Evidence: src/seed.js performs replaceOne/upsert for segments (line 29-31) and then creates indexes after those writes (lines 33-35). The recommended order is to create indexes before bulk seeding to avoid write amplification or unintended write costs.
proposed_change: Create indexes (createIndex) before running upserts/loads, and add a verification step that lists indexes and ensures they exist. Update src/seed.js to createIndex prior to replaceOne.

topic: WriteConcern/readPreference
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Design writeConcern and readPreference intentionally for cross-replica durability or latency needs, but verify Azure DocumentDB's default mapping and supported features first.
proposed_change: A single doc in the product docs that states the supported writeConcern levels, default mapping and sample driver options for Node.js.

topic: Idempotent writes / upsert
detail: Violated: Make writes idempotent or use upsert (e.g., replaceOne / updateOne with upsert: true) so retries do not create duplicates. Evidence: src/seed.js uses upsert replaceOne (line 30) for segments, but src/generate.js inserts campaigns with campaigns.insertOne(doc) (line 85) which can create duplicates on retries.
proposed_change: Use updateOne/replaceOne with an idempotency key or upsert for campaign writes (e.g. include a stable dedupe key or use updateOne({ segmentId, someUniqueKey }, { $set: doc }, { upsert: true })).

topic: Network access restrictions
detail: Violated: Restrict network access to clusters with firewall rules, Private Link (private endpoints) or VNet integration and avoid exposing production cluster endpoints publicly. Evidence: README and scripts do not discuss firewall rules, private endpoints or network security (no guidance present).
proposed_change: Add a security section to README recommending Private Link or firewall rules for production and link to quickstart steps.

topic: Explain & slow-query logging
detail: Violated: Enable slow-query logging and use explain('executionStats') / indexStats to detect COLLSCANs and add appropriate indexes to avoid collection scans. Evidence: No slow-query logging, explain or indexStats verification steps are present in seed/provisioning or README.
proposed_change: Add a small 'verify indexes' step in seed.js that runs explain() on a representative query and logs executionStats, and add a README note on enabling slow-query logging.

topic: Projection for prompt building
detail: Violated: Use projection to fetch only needed fields (partial projection) when building prompts or assembling context to reduce bandwidth, I/O and cost. Evidence: src/generate.js uses segments.findOne({ segmentId }) without projection (line 52) and then JSON.stringify's selected fields into the prompt (lines 58-59).
proposed_change: Use findOne(filter, { projection: { segmentId: 1, name: 1, purchase_history: 1, preferences: 1 } }) to limit returned fields.

topic: Application-level retries
detail: Violated: Implement application-level retries for transient faults but avoid retrying non-idempotent multi-document transactions unless you can guarantee idempotency or use a deduplication token. Evidence: No retry/backoff wrapper is present; campaign writes use insertOne which is not idempotent (src/generate.js line 85).
proposed_change: Add an idempotent write pattern and application-level retry with exponential backoff; avoid retrying the insertOne path or change to upsert with idempotency key.

topic: PII in LLM prompts
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Avoid sending raw PII to LLMs or retaining it in logs; redact or minimize PII in prompts and encrypt or limit sensitive fields at rest.
proposed_change: A one-paragraph policy on the sample README explaining which customer attributes are safe to send to LLMs and an example redaction helper.

proposed_change: Add a maxTimeMS parameter to aggregation_tool and pass it to coll.aggregate(..., maxTimeMS=...) and document defaults in README.

topic: Retries for transient errors
detail: Violated: Use retries for transient errors with exponential backoff and classify errors so non-idempotent operations are not retried blindly. Evidence: No application-level retry wrapper is used for DB writes, fetches, OpenAI calls, or send stubs. app/src/db.js and agents include no retry logic beyond driver configuration.
proposed_change: Wrap critical DB operations and external calls (OpenAI, provider sends) in a retry-with-exponential-backoff helper; limit retries for non-idempotent operations. A minimal change: add a retry(fn, {retries:3, backoffMs:200}) util and use it around getDb operations and send functions.

topic: ESR compound indexes
detail: Violated: Design compound indexes using the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) so abandonment queries (filters + sort) are index-supported and avoid blocking in-memory sorts. Evidence: app/src/db.js line 37 creates index { customerId:1, updatedAt:1, processedAt:1 } but the abandonment query (app/src/index.js lines 9-16) does not filter by customerId; because the equality prefix is absent the index cannot serve the sort by updatedAt, risking a collection scan.
proposed_change: Create an index that matches the actual query shape, e.g., { updatedAt: -1, processedAt: 1 } (or a separate index on updatedAt) so the query filter and sort are index-supported, or add customerId equality to query if appropriate.

topic: Projections / covered queries
detail: Violated: Use projections and covered queries to return only fields needed for orchestration to reduce network and memory usage; design covering indexes when appropriate. Evidence: app/src/index.js line 16 uses carts.find(query).sort(...).toArray() without a projection; the orchestration only needs a small set of fields (cartId, customerId, items, updatedAt).
proposed_change: Add a projection to the find call: .find(query, { projection: { cartId:1, customerId:1, items:1, updatedAt:1 } }) to reduce network payload and memory usage.

topic: Explain and slow-query logging
detail: Violated: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logging, route logs to Log Analytics, and use explain("executionStats") to identify COLLSCANs and high docsExamined to guide index changes. Evidence: No calls to explain() or diagnostic-setting configuration were made during seeding or verification (events.jsonl does not show explain operations).
proposed_change: Add an explain() check to the seed/CI that runs the abandonment query with explain('executionStats') and fails or warns when the plan shows COLLSCAN or high docsExamined; document how to enable diagnostic settings in README.

topic: Least-privilege access

topic: Use explain() for query performance

topic: Vector-index creation and embedding-dimension guidance for samples

Effect: The sample computes embeddings but does not create a vector index. As a result, embedding-based retrieval cannot be verified end-to-end without manual index creation, which the builder flagged in verification.
proposed_change: [mcp_tool_or_description] Add to the documentdb-vector-search skill a seed-snippet and a sample src/seed-vector-index.js that reads EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIM from env and runs createIndexes/createSearchIndexes with a minimal HNSW (or IVF) config for demos, plus a README section on scaling these parameters.

topic: Normalize vendor name guidance and a canonical field
detail: Missing: Public, easily discoverable guidance recommending storing a normalized vendor field (vendor_normalized) at write-time for reliable indexed equality lookups, with a small code example. Looked in: Indexing and query docs; the pattern is commonly used in prior knowledge but not shown as a concise recipe in DocumentDB quickstarts. Effect: The app implements runtime normalization for scoring but does not persist a normalized field, which prevents efficient indexed equality lookups and makes some queries rely on regex that may not use indexes.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short page: 'Canonicalizing and indexing free-text keys (vendor names)' with code examples (Mongoose middleware to set vendor_normalized) and an index recommendation. Example: add pre('save') hook to set vendor_normalized = normalize(vendorName) and create compound index on vendor_normalized + totalAmount.

topic: Recommendation for monetary types (Decimal128 or integer cents)
detail: Missing: An explicit sample-recommendation page stating 'store money as Decimal128 or integer cents with examples in Mongoose' for DocumentDB. For financial examples this risks precision issues and is not best-practice.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] Short doc 'Representing money' with Mongoose examples (Decimal128 field or integer cents), seeding examples, and migration notes.

topic: Agent memory persistence choices
detail: Missing: A short page/rule explaining the tradeoffs between in-process ephemeral session memory vs persisted memory (DocumentDB or Redis) for agent corrections, and a recommended default for gallery samples. Looked in: No single DocumentDB doc covers agent memory; this is application-level guidance missing from product docs. Effect: Implementer defaulted to an in-process Map (ephemeral). That meets 'within a session' but is easy to misuse in multi-process deployments.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] A short note in the agent kit: 'Use ephemeral memory for single-process demos; use persistent store (DocumentDB/Redis) if you want cross-process persistence; provide examples for both.'

topic: TLS & auth config
detail: Violated: Use TLS in the MongoDB connection string (tls=true) and a secure authentication mechanism (SCRAM-SHA-256 or Microsoft Entra ID) and avoid accepting invalid certificates in production. Evidence: app/src/db.js sets options = { dbName } only (lines 12-15) and does not set TLS or certificate validation options or explicit retry/timeouts. The .env.example instructs to set a connection string but does not document required TLS options.
proposed_change: Add recommended connection options to db.js (e.g., ensure the connection string includes tls=true / tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false if applicable, set serverSelectionTimeoutMS and appropriate pool settings) and document when to use Microsoft Entra ID. Prefer adding default, safe connection options in the documentdb-connection skill so all samples use them.

topic: Driver retries
detail: Violated: Evaluate the driver's retryableWrites option (samples often set retryWrites=false) and design application-level retries and idempotency carefully so retries don't cause duplicate side effects. Evidence: app/src/db.js does not set retryWrites, retryReads, serverSelectionTimeoutMS or other retry-related driver settings (options only contains dbName at lines 12-15). No application-level retry wrappers exist for DB writes in the reconciliation paths.
proposed_change: Add driver options (e.g., retryWrites=false where recommended) and wrap non-idempotent writes with application-level retry/ idempotency keys; add a short rule to documentdb-connection skill to set safe defaults for samples.

topic: Compound index for vendor+amount
detail: Violated: Create compound indexes for queries that filter on multiple fields (for example vendor + amount) so the predicate can use an index rather than scanning the collection. Evidence: PurchaseOrder and Invoice models index vendorName and totalAmount individually (app/src/models/purchaseOrder.js lines 10-12 and app/src/models/invoice.js lines 10-12), but there is no compound index on vendor+totalAmount. Some queries use regexes that can prevent index use (app/src/reconciler.js line 42 uses vendorName regex without an anchor).
proposed_change: Add a compound index on { vendorName: 1, totalAmount: 1 } (create in seed script or model definition) or store a normalized vendor field and index { vendor_normalized: 1, totalAmount: 1 }. Prefer adding a documentdb-indexing skill rule advising compound indexes for matching workloads.

topic: Limit returned fields / batchSize
detail: Violated: Limit returned fields with projections and use cursor batchSize when scanning candidate sets to reduce network and deserialization cost. Evidence: PurchaseOrder.find calls do not use projection or batchSize in app/src/reconciler.js (line 42-45) and app/src/reconcile.js (line 17), which returns full documents and their lineItems even though scoring only requires id, vendorName and totalAmount.
proposed_change: Use .find(query, { poNumber:1, vendorName:1, totalAmount:1 }) and consider .cursor().batchSize(...) for large candidate sets; update findCandidatesByInvoice to project only needed fields.

topic: Server-side aggregation for heavy scoring
detail: Violated: When scoring candidates at scale, use server-side aggregation pipelines (match/project/limit early) so you reduce documents transferred and only fetch the fields required for scoring. Evidence: The sample performs client-side scoring by loading candidates and computing scores in JS (app/src/reconciler.js lines 47-65). No aggregation pipeline usage is present.
proposed_change: If scaling beyond demos, move prefiltering and projection into an aggregation pipeline (match / project / limit) and only return fields required for scoring. Document this pattern in documentdb-query-optimizer skill.

topic: Avoid leading-wildcard regex
detail: Violated: Avoid expensive regex and string-function queries for matching; normalize values on write (case) or use indexed fields / text search, and avoid leading-wildcard regexes because they prevent index use. Evidence: app/src/reconciler.js line 42 uses vendorName: { $regex: new RegExp(vendor, 'i') } (no anchor) which can cause collection scans; app/src/reconcile.js line 10 uses an anchored regex (^... ) which is index-friendly. The code is inconsistent.
proposed_change: Normalize vendor names on write and use equality or anchored regexes; add normalized vendor field and index it. Update findCandidatesByInvoice to use anchored regex or vendor_normalized equality.

topic: Monetary storage type
detail: Violated: Use Decimal128 (or integer cents) to store monetary values instead of IEEE floats; Azure DocumentDB supports Decimal128 BSON type. Evidence: Invoice and PurchaseOrder schemas store totalAmount as Number (app/src/models/invoice.js line 12 and app/src/models/purchaseOrder.js line 12) which maps to JS Number (IEEE float) rather than Decimal128 or integer cents.
proposed_change: Store monetary amounts as integer cents or use mongoose.Schema.Types.Decimal128 and index that field. Update seed and models to use Decimal128 or a cents integer field.

topic: Normalize vendor on write
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Normalize vendor names on write (e.g., lowercase/trim/canonicalize) if you need reliable equality or indexed lookups rather than relying on ad-hoc regex at query time.
proposed_change: A sentence in the 'Data modeling' quickstart showing 'store vendor_normalized = vendorName.toLowerCase().trim().replace(/[\W_]+/g, "") and index it' would let agents implement this reliably.

topic: Embedding metadata
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Record embedding metadata (dimension and model version) in your application documents to detect incompatible embeddings before re-indexing.
proposed_change: A short 'Embedding metadata' paragraph in the vector-search quickstart describing storing { embeddingModel, embeddingDimensions } per doc.

topic: Bulk upload ordered:false guidance (prior knowledge gap)
detail: Missing: No authoritative Azure DocumentDB-specific guidance was found for using unordered/bulkWrite (ordered:false) inserts when ingesting many documents; searches returned Cosmos DB for MongoDB guidance or generic MongoDB guidance but not DocumentDB-specific docs. Looked in: learn.microsoft.com (DocumentDB vector search, quickstarts), agent kit skills, events.jsonl searches for 'ordered: false' and related terms. Effect: The builder could not rely on a DocumentDB-specific recommendation for using unordered bulk writes; this affects seed script design decisions (batch sizes and error semantics) and may lead the author to pick a pattern based on non-DocumentDB sources.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short 'Bulk ingestion' guidance page under Azure DocumentDB ingestion docs describing batch size recommendations, whether insertMany/BulkWrite supports ordered:false and best-practice error semantics for large-scale ingestion; include example code for Python/pymongo with recommended batch sizes for M10/M20/M30 tiers.

topic: Optimistic concurrency / etag guidance for DocumentDB
detail: Missing: No DocumentDB-specific documentation was found describing etag/_etag or an official optimistic concurrency pattern for upserts in the vCore-managed DocumentDB offering (searches returned Cosmos DB pages but not DocumentDB-specific ones). Looked in: learn.microsoft.com search for 'etag', 'optimistic concurrency' and 'DocumentDB' (events.jsonl shows searches around these terms), agent-kit resources. Effect: Unclear guidance increases the risk of creating non-idempotent seed scripts or unsafe update patterns; the builder cannot confidently pick a safe concurrency approach without potentially using the wrong semantics.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short page describing optimistic concurrency options for Azure DocumentDB, whether an _etag-like mechanism is exposed to the MongoDB API, and patterns for idempotent upserts including example pymongo code.

topic: Embedding model + index-dimension guidance (discoverability)
detail: Missing: The sample must choose an embedding model and then create the index with matching dimensions. While the docs explain how to create indexes they do not present a short 'choose an embedding model and set EMBEDDING_DIM' cookbook for sample authors. Looked in: learn.microsoft.com vector-search pages and agent-kit vector-search skill resources (events.jsonl). Effect: The builder picked text-embedding-3-small and EMBEDDING_DIM=1536 by model default; without a clear example in docs, other authors may mismatch model dims and index dimensions and cause index creation/query failures.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add a short 'Embedding model to index dimension' note to the vector-search quickstart: list common embedding models and dims (e.g., text-embedding-3-small=1536, text-embedding-3-large=3072), and show the exact JSON snippet for createSearchIndexes using dimensions=${EMBEDDING_DIM}.

topic: Citation/grounding format for RAG responses
detail: Missing: The starter prompt requested 'grounded answers' but did not specify a citation format (inline bracketed id, list of sources array, show product_id/chunk_id, etc.). No authoritative sample guidance states the preferred citation format for DocumentDB-backed RAG samples. Looked in: agent-kit skills, vector-search docs, sample gallery guidance; events.jsonl searches for 'citation format' and 'grounding' returned no definitive template. Effect: Without a specified citation format the builder may omit explicit identifiers or produce inconsistent grounding; test harnesses expecting product_id/chunk_id in the LLM output cannot assert structure.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Add an agent-kit rule for gallery RAG samples: require answers to include a 'sources' list with objects {product_id, chunk_id, source_type, score} and an inline bracketing style like '[source: product_id:chunk_id]' where the LLM can insert at each supporting sentence.

topic: Unit tests that run offline (how-to)
detail: Missing: No public sample pattern documenting how to author unit tests for DocumentDB-backed vector stores that run without a live cluster (mocking pymongo, embedding provider, and the LlamaIndex vector store). Looked in: learn.microsoft.com, agent-kit skills, quickstarts; searches for 'unit tests mock pymongo' returned examples for other services but not a concise pattern for DocumentDB + vector stores. Effect: The reference expects offline tests but the builder had no guidance on mocking DocumentDB vector features and searchScore projection; this raises barrier for test authors and may cause them to skip tests or write brittle integration tests.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] A short 'Testing' appendix showing pytest examples that mock pymongo.collection.Collection.find/aggregate, stub embedding calls, and assert LlamaIndex uses precomputed vectors; include a template 'tests/test_seed.py' and 'tests/test_api.py' using pytest-mock.

topic: Naming clarification: Azure DocumentDB vs Cosmos DB
detail: Missing: The product naming has historically caused confusion. The team should publish a short, prominent naming note clarifying 'Azure DocumentDB (vCore-managed mongoClusters) vs Azure Cosmos DB (databaseAccounts, RU-based) vs Amazon DocumentDB'. Looked in: readiness findings and cold-answers revealed multiple confusions (readiness_findings S02..S05), and developer-run searches in events.jsonl returned both mongoClusters and databaseAccounts pages. Effect: Naming confusion can cause authors to pick the wrong CLI commands, resource types or example connection strings (e.g., using mongodb://:10255 instead of mongodb+srv).
proposed_change: [naming_or_disambiguation] A short 'Which product is this?' note at the top of DocumentDB quickstarts and the sample README: show correct resource type (Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters), example CLI group (az documentdb mongocluster), SRV connection-string examples and portal steps.

topic: Prior-knowledge-only practices (bulk inserts, optimistic concurrency)
detail: Missing: Two discovered items (bulk insert ordered:false and optimistic concurrency / _etag) had no DocumentDB-specific public docs and were marked prior_knowledge_only by the discovery agent. Looked in: learn.microsoft.com searches (events.jsonl) and agent-kit docs. Effect: Agents may apply MongoDB or Cosmos DB patterns that do not precisely apply to Azure DocumentDB and cause incorrect ingestion or update logic.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] Add short clarifications in the ingestion and data-modeling docs that state whether unordered bulkWrite is supported and how optimistic concurrency should be implemented (or a note that drivers' Mongo semantics apply), with code examples for pymongo.

topic: Singleton MongoClient
detail: Violated: Use a single MongoClient per process (singleton) and reuse it across requests; in serverless environments initialize the client outside the function handler to enable connection reuse and avoid pool exhaustion. Evidence: No db client module found in workspace; documentdb-driver skill loaded (events.jsonl) and driver-singleton-client.md was read, but the workspace contains no implementation files (03-build.md lines 5, 53).
proposed_change: Create src/db.py exporting a singleton MongoClient (instantiate once at module import) and use it across the app.

topic: Vector index creation
detail: Violated: When using DocumentDB's integrated vector features, create and query vector indexes with the `cosmosSearch` operator (vector-diskann / vector-hnsw / vector-ivf) and tune index parameters such as dimensions, similarity (COS/L2/IP), lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree/efConstruction to match dataset size and recall/latency targets. Evidence: No index-creation code or createSearchIndexes payload present; build report notes index creation planned but not executed (03-build.md lines 30-33, 55).
proposed_change: Add index-creation logic using createIndexes/createSearchIndexes with cosmosSearchOptions.kind and dimensions read from EMBEDDING_DIM; include default HNSW parameters for demo corpus.

topic: Store embedding field type
detail: Violated: Store embeddings as numeric arrays on a dedicated field (e.g., embedding: number[]) and create a vector index for that field (one vector index per path) rather than indexing embeddings as text. Evidence: No ingestion code; no documents in repo and no schema examples committed. Build notes describe storing embedding but no code exists (03-build.md lines 26-33).
proposed_change: When inserting chunk documents, include a numeric embedding array in field 'embedding' and create a vector index on that path.

topic: Chunking long documents
detail: Violated: When building RAG, chunk long documents before embedding and vectorizing; use token-aware chunking (start around 512 tokens ≈ 2000 characters) with overlap (e.g., ~25%) and record chunk metadata (parent_id/product_id, chunk_id, source, token_count) to enable selective retrieval and prompt-budgeting. Evidence: No seed/chunking code present; build report lists chunking as a design goal but not implemented (03-build.md lines 26-28).
proposed_change: Implement token-aware chunker (e.g., use tiktoken) with overlap and persist chunk metadata: product_id, chunk_id, token_count, source_type.

topic: Top-k retrieval and trimming
detail: Violated: At query time, request a top-k (e.g., k=5) vector result set from the vector index and then apply metadata filters and a lightweight reranker or token-budget-aware trimming (using stored token_count) to select which chunks to include in the LLM prompt. Evidence: No retrieval or reranking code present; build report planned top-5 retrieval but not implemented (03-build.md lines 26-39, 56).
proposed_change: Implement retriever to fetch top-5, then apply token-budget-aware trimming/reranking using stored token_count before prompt construction.

topic: Index type by scale
detail: Violated: Choose vector index type by scale: use vector-ivf for small datasets, vector-hnsw up to moderate scale (tens of thousands), and prefer DiskANN for high-scale production workloads (hundreds of thousands+); tune nlist/M/efConstruction/lBuild/lSearch and consider product quantization or fp16 for high-dimensional vectors. Evidence: Events show the vector-search skill and 'vector-choose-index-type' resource were read (events.jsonl). The builder planned HNSW for demo but no index creation code exists (events show failed log attempt; 03-build.md lines 30-33).
proposed_change: Document the default (vector-hnsw) for demo and provide README guidance to switch to vector-ivf or vector-diskann for other scales; implement index creation with these defaults.

topic: Normalize embeddings
detail: Violated: Normalize embeddings at ingestion (L2 / unit-length) when you use cosine similarity, and store the embedding model name, dimensions, and a version in the document so you can detect model drift and reindex safely. Evidence: documentdb-vector-search skill resources (vector-normalize-embeddings.md) were read (events.jsonl), but no ingestion code normalizing embeddings or storing embedding metadata exists in workspace.
proposed_change: Normalize embeddings at ingestion and persist metadata fields embeddingModel, embeddingDims, embeddingVersion in each chunk document.

topic: Create search indexes programmatically
detail: Violated: Use the MCP/documentdb toolset or SDKs to list collections and indexes, create vector and search indexes programmatically (createIndexes / createSearchIndexes or runCommand), and to retrieve searchScore (`$meta: "searchScore"`) when projecting $search results. Evidence: Events show search of vector index docs and the MCP skill loaded; no index-creation code exists in the workspace and no projection of searchScore implemented (03-build.md lines 30-33, 55).
proposed_change: Add code or an MCP/az CLI script to create the index and in retrieval include projection of { score: { $meta: 'searchScore' } } so the similarity score is returned.

topic: Metadata for chunks
detail: Violated: Store provenance and enrichment metadata (source, page/chunk index, embeddingModel, embeddingDims, embeddingVersion, token_count) for each chunk so retrieval, filtering, re-embedding and auditing are possible. Evidence: No ingestion code exists to show metadata is persisted; build notes planned metadata but not implemented (03-build.md lines 26-33).
proposed_change: Persist the listed metadata fields for each chunk during ingestion (product_id, chunk_id, token_count, embeddingModel, embeddingDims, embeddingVersion, source_type).

topic: TLS required
detail: Violated: Always require TLS for DocumentDB connections (ensure tls=true and SCRAM-SHA-256 in connection string) and do not disable certificate validation in production. Evidence: documentdb-security and driver skills were loaded (events.jsonl), but no connection code is present to show TLS options are set; no files in workspace.
proposed_change: Ensure connection URIs and client options require tls/tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false in production; document dev exceptions for local gateway only.

topic: Secrets handling
detail: Violated: Prefer managed identity / Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC or Key Vault references to long-lived connection credentials in production and never commit connection strings or secrets to source control; read connection strings from environment variables or secret stores at runtime. Evidence: No .env.example nor code showing environment variable reads; build report instructs to set env vars but files were not created (03-build.md lines 14-21, 53).
proposed_change: Add .env.example and ensure code reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from env; include guidance to use Key Vault or managed identities for production.

topic: Retries and backoff
detail: Violated: Implement retries for transient errors with exponential backoff and jitter and honor server-provided retry signals (e.g., 429 Retry-After) rather than immediate aggressive retries. Evidence: documentdb-connection skill read (events.jsonl). No client retry wrappers or retry logic code present in workspace.
proposed_change: Wrap DocumentDB calls with retry logic using exponential backoff and jitter; honor Retry-After and surface errors to client when retries exhausted.

topic: Client timeouts
detail: Violated: Apply minimal tunings to client timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) appropriate to the workload: short for fail-fast server selection, longer for expected long-running analytical queries. Evidence: documentdb-connection skill resources were inspected (events.jsonl). No client config code exists to show timeouts set.
proposed_change: Set sensible default timeouts in the MongoClient creation and make them configurable via env vars (e.g., SERVER_SELECTION_TIMEOUT_MS, SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS).

topic: Audit trail: vector-index choice
detail: Violated: Builder chose vector-hnsw for the demo vector index, but this choice did not end up as a recorded successful decision entry. Evidence: events.jsonl contains failed attempts to log the vector-hnsw choice (failed log_decision events at timestamps ~05:54:21 - 05:54:27 indicating validation error), but no matching decision appears in decisions.jsonl. See events.jsonl entries around the failed log_decision calls.
proposed_change: Record the index-choice decision properly into decisions.jsonl (reason_source should be one of allowed values) or include the rationale in the build report so readers can audit the choice.

topic: Retries & idempotency
detail: Violated: Handle transient faults by implementing retries with exponential backoff and making write operations idempotent. Evidence: No explicit retry-with-backoff wrapper for DB operations. update_price_tool uses find_one_and_update (atomic) which helps idempotency, but there is no retry policy around DB calls and seed uses simple insert/update without exponential backoff.
proposed_change: Wrap DB calls (writes and critical reads) with a small retry policy using exponential backoff (e.g., tenacity) and make non-idempotent writes detect unknown outcomes (or use idempotent upserts).

topic: Use projections
detail: Violated: Use projections (select only required fields) on find/aggregate queries to reduce network payload and RU consumption when you don't need full documents. Evidence: get_competitor_prices_tool (app/agent.py lines 38-41) calls coll.find(...) without a projection, which fetches full documents although only price, source, and timestamp are used in the summary. Similarly, get_margin_rules_tool uses find_one and serializes the whole document (app/agent.py lines 101-116, 120-126).
proposed_change: Add projections to find calls (e.g., coll.find(filter, { 'price': 1, 'source': 1, 'timestamp': 1 })) and to find_one where only specific fields are needed.

topic: Optimistic concurrency
detail: Violated: Implement optimistic concurrency control using system _etag (ETag) or a version field and conditional updates. Evidence: README.md line 54 explicitly notes the sample 'does not implement optimistic concurrency control.' update_price_tool uses a single atomic update but does not filter by _etag or version (app/agent.py lines 143-147).
proposed_change: Implement an optional optimistic concurrency pattern: include a version field or read _etag and include it in the update filter (e.g., {'sku': sku, '_etag': current_etag}) and surface a retry/failure path if the update fails due to a mismatch.

proposed_change: A short sentence in the 'security' quickstart: 'Do not pass connection strings or keys to an LLM; expose DB queries via parameterized tools.'

topic: Cap transitions
detail: Violated: Avoid unbounded growth of in-document arrays (like transitions); cap the array or move history into a separate transitions collection. Evidence: app/src/models.py:22 defines transitions: List[Transition] = [] with no cap; app/src/orchestrator.py:62-66 pushes transitions with no slice/cap.
proposed_change: Change the atomic update to cap entries (example: use $push with $each and $slice) or store transitions in a separate collection. Minimal code fix: in _transition_atomic use {'$push': {'transitions': {'$each': [transition], '$slice': -100}}} to keep last 100 entries.

topic: Index for work discovery
detail: Violated: Create an index to efficiently find work: at minimum create a compound index on state plus a scheduling or ordering field; make application_id unique if you query by it. Evidence: app/src/models.py:20 declares current_state Indexed(str) (index implied). The sample runner queries by applicant.ssn_last4 (app/run_orchestrator.py:16) but there is no index on applicant.ssn_last4 declared; transitions.timestamp index not created programmatically.
proposed_change: Add an index on applicant.ssn_last4 (and/or create a unique application_id index). Example: in init_db or seed call coll.create_index([('applicant.ssn_last4',1)], name='idx_ssn_last4'). Also consider a compound index {current_state:1, next_action_at:1} if scheduling is added.

topic: Beanie model registration and indexes

topic: Backoff and retries
detail: Violated: Use exponential backoff with jitter for application-level retries on transient errors. Evidence: app/src/db.py creates an AsyncIOMotorClient without configuring retry/backoff strategies and orchestrator methods do not wrap DB calls with retry loops.
proposed_change: Add a retry wrapper with exponential backoff/jitter for transient errors (e.g., use tenacity or implement an async retry decorator) and make DB operations idempotent where retries may occur.

topic: Project only required fields
detail: Violated: Keep documents small and project only required fields in queries. Evidence: run_orchestrator.py:24-26 prints full document returned by coll.find_one and the orchestrator re-reads the whole document; queries fetch entire documents rather than projecting only required fields.
proposed_change: When listing pending work or reading only state consider projecting only necessary fields (e.g., coll.find_one({'_id': id}, projection={'current_state':1, 'applicant.name':1, 'applicant.ssn_last4':1})).
