topic: Env example completeness
detail: Missing: .env.example omitted a few runtime variables used or commonly needed for a sample (PORT, LOG_LEVEL and a note about DATABASE_NAME). Looked in: Repository files (.env.example, src/db.js) and quickstart docs for Mongoose on DocumentDB. Effect: Minor: the sample ran because defaults exist (PORT defaulted to 3000); however users/agents might not know which env vars are optional vs required.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] Short README subsection and an updated .env.example listing: DOCUMENTDB_URI (placeholder), DATABASE_NAME (placeholder), PORT (placeholder, default 3000), LOG_LEVEL (optional), and notes indicating which are optional and where to get the connection string. Add a one-line example `DOCUMENTDB_URI="mongodb+srv://<user>:<pass>@<cluster>.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com/?tls=true&authMechanism=SCRAM-SHA-256&retryWrites=false"`.

topic: Which Mongoose version to pin
detail: Missing: Authoritative guidance in the quickstarts about which Mongoose major version is recommended/pinned for DocumentDB + Node 24. Looked in: learn.microsoft.com quickstarts and tutorial pages. The quickstarts recommend Mongoose 9 in several examples, but the sample used Mongoose 7.x without explicit guidance in the agent kit. Effect: Medium: the builder chose Mongoose 7.x (logged D002). Using a non-tested Mongoose major can cause subtle incompatibilities or confuse agents when choosing a runtime.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add a short 'tested versions' box in the Node/Mongoose quickstarts listing a tested Mongoose version (e.g. 9.12.1) and tested MongoDB driver bundle, plus notes on which older Mongoose majors are supported. Also add a one-line recommendation in the agent-kit templates to pin the tested version in package.json.

topic: DocumentDB vs Cosmos DB naming/disambiguation
detail: Missing: Clear, prominent guidance distinguishing 'Azure DocumentDB (managed MongoDB-compatible vCore offering)' from 'Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (RU-based)' and from Amazon DocumentDB. The readiness findings show agents and builders confuse resource names, CLI groups and template resource types. Looked in: Learn docs and agent-kit readiness notes; several quickstarts historically show Cosmos DB 'databaseAccounts' which caused confusion with the mongoClusters resource type. Effect: High risk: confusion leads to wrong IaC templates (databaseAccounts vs mongoClusters), the wrong az CLI group (az cosmosdb vs az documentdb), wrong connection strings/ports, and incorrect guidance to agents.
proposed_change: [naming_or_disambiguation] A single-line prominent banner at the top of relevant quickstarts and the agent-kit README: 'Azure DocumentDB (mongoClusters) is distinct from Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (databaseAccounts RU) and from Amazon DocumentDB — use Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters and az documentdb mongocluster commands for DocumentDB clusters.' Include quick examples of the correct az command and a Bicep snippet showing Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters.

topic: Vector index createIndexes examples
detail: Missing: Copy/paste createIndexes runCommand examples for HNSW/IVF/DiskANN with the exact cosmosSearchOptions field names and sample parameters. Looked in: Vector search docs on learn.microsoft.com; readiness notes flagged that agents guess vendor-neutral syntax and can be rejected by the server. Effect: Medium for vector-enabled samples; low for this sample because it doesn't use vectors. Without explicit examples agents will attempt incorrect createIndex syntax and receive errors.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A small 'indexing' snippet page showing db.runCommand({ createIndexes: '<coll>', indexes:[{ key:{'<field>':'cosmosSearch'}, name:'vec', cosmosSearchOptions:{ kind:'vector-hnsw', dimensions:1536, similarity:'COS', m:16, efConstruction:64 } }] }) for each supported kind, plus notes on dimension matching and retryWrites=false requirement.

topic: Idempotency operational guidance
detail: Missing: There is no single public page that specifies idempotency-key canonicalization (length, allowed characters) or retention/cleanup guidance for billing audit records for Azure DocumentDB. Looked in: Learn docs and discovered_practices search; several 'searches_with_no_useful_result' entries listed idempotency-key length and retention guidance. Effect: Low: the sample uses a simple string idempotencyKey and demonstrates the technique, but agents building production systems may pick unsafe key formats or retention policies.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] Add a short 'Idempotency for billing' page: recommend idempotencyKey canonical form (UUID or application-provided stable identifier), a unique index, recommended retention for audit records, and examples of how to expire/compact old audit data.

topic: Testing without live cluster
detail: Missing: Guidance and an example test-suite showing how to run unit tests without a live DocumentDB cluster (example using mongodb-memory-server or Mongoose mocking). Looked in: Quickstarts and agent-kit docs — no dedicated test example for DocumentDB Mongoose samples. Effect: Medium: the repository contains no tests; adding example tests would make the sample suitable for CI and gallery submission.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] A short 'Testing' page in the sample template that includes an example Jest/Mocha test that runs with mongodb-memory-server and demonstrates mocking transactions and idempotency behavior, plus a note describing what needs a live cluster (index verification).

topic: TTL verification & testing guidance
detail: Missing: A short documented note on TTL behavior (how expireAfterSeconds works, background thread timing, and how to test it deterministically in CI or locally). Looked in: learn.microsoft.com TTL docs and sample scripts; TTL semantics (background job) are documented but a short testing cookbook for builders is missing. Effect: Low: the index was created but automatic deletion was not observed during the run because TTL is time-based.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A one-paragraph note in the TTL docs: explain that expireAfterSeconds is applied relative to the indexed Date, deletion is performed by a background thread (may take minutes), and provide a testing recipe (set a near-future expiresAt and wait or simulate clock in local gateway) and how to verify deletions via listIndexes and count queries.

topic: Indexes for query patterns
detail: Violated: Create indexes to match your query patterns (equality → sort → range ordering) and verify index usage with explain('executionStats') to avoid collection scans. Evidence: scripts/create_indexes.js created a unique idempotencyKey and an index on ChargeEvent.customerId but did not explicitly create an index on ChargeEvent.subscriptionId (schema defines subscriptionId: index: true in app/src/models/chargeEvent.js line 5, but autoIndex is disabled in app/src/db.js line 22 so the schema index will not be created automatically).
proposed_change: Add creation of an index on subscriptionId in scripts/create_indexes.js (e.g. await ChargeEvent.collection.createIndex({ subscriptionId: 1 }, { name: 'idx_charge_subscriptionId' })); or re-enable autoIndex during index-creation/deployment only.

topic: Retries and idempotency
detail: Violated: Implement bounded retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and ensure retries are safe (idempotent) or protected by the idempotency key rather than blindly reissuing non-idempotent writes. Evidence: The sample does not implement bounded retries or exponential backoff; error handling is present and the idempotency key protects against duplicate processing, but there's no retry/backoff wrapper for transient failures.
proposed_change: Add a small retry wrapper with exponential backoff for transient connection/write errors (respecting idempotency keys) or use a retry library and document which errors are safe to retry.
